content:
Mia Chen: FYI we just got an escalation from AcmeApp — Console trace view shows requests that have no spans attached and the link from request_id -> trace opens a blank trace page. Customer says this started after last week's runtime release.

AcmeApp details they submitted: request_id=req-20260317-9a1b, sample trace link: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace-0x4f5a2c (shows empty). They can reproduce consistently for a subset of requests.

Mia Chen: Repro steps provided by customer:
1) curl -i -H "x-request-id: req-20260317-9a1b" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
2) Wait for Console to index -> traces tab -> search by request id -> click result (blank trace).

Mia Chen: Attached sample headers/log snippet from their side:
```
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] request_id=req-20260317-9a1b method=POST path=/v1/generate status=200 traceparent=  user_agent=acme-integration/1.2.0
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] span_start trace_id=trace-0x4f5a2c span_id=span-0x1a parent_id= span_name=api.request
```

Jordan Rivera: Looking. My first guess is the collector or ingestion pipeline dropping spans where parent_id is empty — console expects parent/child links to render waterfall. If the agent stopped forwarding `traceparent` headers last week due to the header whitelist change, we could see that.

Liam Patel: Noted. I pushed a runtime change last Wednesday that introduced stricter header sanitization in the gateway. It strips headers not in the allowlist. Could be x-request-id or traceparent getting stripped before the otel exporter sees them.

Pauline Gomez: Customer said it started after runtime update — sounds like a likely correlate. Can we confirm whether the gateway strip occurred in ingress?

Jordan Rivera: Quick check in the collector logs shows a lot of spans arriving without parent_id around that timeframe. Sample from spans store:
```
{ "trace_id": "trace-0x4f5a2c", "span_id": "span-0x1a", "parent_id": null, "name": "api.request", "timestamp": "2026-03-17T14:02:11Z" }
{ "trace_id": "trace-0x4f5a2c", "span_id": "span-0x1b", "parent_id": null, "name": "db.query", "timestamp": "2026-03-17T14:02:11Z" }
```
This matches the blank/flat trace in UI.

ingest-bot: Ingest backlog shows a spike of 7k partial traces between 2026-03-16 22:00 UTC and 2026-03-17 02:00 UTC with parent_id == null.

Liam Patel: Confirmed the gateway change: the header allowlist omitted `traceparent` and `tracestate` when the stricter policy landed. The downstream otel exporter didn't get the trace context, so spans were emitted without parents. That explains the missing links.

Mia Chen: Customer wants ETA on fix and whether we can backfill their traces. They're not blocked on production but analytics and trace-based alerts are broken.

Jordan Rivera: Plan: (1) Hotfix gateway to stop stripping trace headers (roll back header sanitization rule) — target in 30m. (2) Run a re-join job to re-link spans where possible: re-ingest pipeline can correlate by request_id -> trace_id mapping if the original request headers were logged in ingress. (3) Console UI fallback: show "Partial trace — some spans missing" and surface raw logs for request_id while backfill runs.

Liam Patel: I'll open a patch PR to restore trace headers and cut a canary. If approved will deploy to canary region first. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/runtime/merge_requests/342 — includes tests ensuring traceparent is preserved.

Pauline Gomez: For customer comms: propose we say root cause is header sanitization in runtime that prevented trace context propagation. ETA: rollback + canary in 1h, full rollout 3h after verification, backfill job TBD (depends on how many requests need re-linking).

Mia Chen: I'm sending an update to AcmeApp now — will include repro, mitigations, and expected timeline.

Jordan Rivera: Re: backfill — ops runbook (short):
1) Query logs for request_id -> find original trace_id assignment (if any): `SELECT request_id, trace_id FROM ingress_logs WHERE request_time BETWEEN '2026-03-16' AND '2026-03-17' AND request_id LIKE 'req-%'`
2) For each mapping, call internal relink job: `python ops/relink_spans.py --trace-id <trace_id> --request-id <request_id>`
3) Reindex into traces table and refresh materialized view: `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_traces;`

Liam Patel: Will also add a short-term telemetry alert: if >5% traces have parent_id == null across a 30m window, trigger pager. Added to eng-sre alert rules in PR 87.

Mia Chen: Customer replied: "Thanks — appreciate the quick update. Can you confirm that no billing or inference result correctness was affected?"

Pauline Gomez: Confirmed: only observability (Console traces) affected. Generation and billing unaffected.

Jordan Rivera: Follow-ups: (a) run canary rollback, (b) kick off relink job for affected orgs (priority: AcmeApp), (c) add UI fallback and message. I'll coordinate with ops on the relink window.

Mia Chen: Thanks team. I'll keep thread updated and paste logs from relink job here once it's started. :thumbsup:

ingest-bot: Relink job queued for org AcmeApp (job id rl-20260317-77). Estimated time 45m.

Mia Chen: Relink started — first batch processed ~1200 traces, ~70% successfully re-linked, attaching sample trace link: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace-0x4f5a2c (now shows partial waterfall).

Pauline Gomez: Good progress. Let's track completion and then notify customer with final summary and RCA doc.

Mia Chen: Noted — will draft RCA after closure.
